nodes.n: The other side of the world. It has rained for three days. The hotel window shows a grey city, a church spire, and your own tired face.

nodes.t: My terms. When Raghav goes down, my name stays out of every report. And my agency gets your contract. Clean, no Mehra money.
In return I give you his second phone. The one he texts players from. I can clone it in a night.

choice.t: "I don't make deals with Mehra's people."

nodes.t: Give me two days. And don't look at me in public. You're terrible at hiding things.

nodes.n: Video call home. It's 4 AM in Rajgarh. Maa answers anyway, in the dark.

msgs.t: Are you eating? You look thin. The camera makes you thin or you are thin?
Papa is sleeping in the stall now. With the policeman. They play cards.
Come home safe. Cricket can wait. Safe can't.

nodes.n: A knock. Vikrant, in a hoodie, soaked from the corridor's broken skylight.

nodes.t: Before you say anything, I'm not here to fight. I'm here because my father works for Raghav Mehra now.
Chauhan Construction builds his stadiums. I heard them on the phone in Lucknow. They were talking about the final. And about Karan.
I'll say it to the integrity people. On one condition. I bat at four in the final. Not you.

choice.t: "You'd sell the truth for a batting slot?"

nodes.t: Whatever you need, I'll say it. On record. He's my father. But Karan's son is seven.

nodes.n: A crash from the room next door. Karan's room. Shouting, then nothing.
You push open his door. He's on the floor with his phone. On the screen: a video call. A small boy in a school uniform, crying. A stranger's hand resting on his shoulder.

nodes.t: Veer. Veer, look at Papa. Look at me, beta. It's okay.

nodes.n: The call ends. One text arrives. "Do the catch, captain."

nodes.cliff: They've stopped threatening Karan's son. They're standing next to him.
